description: Project Uriel es un equipo costarricense enfocado en desarrollo de software, análisis de datos, inteligencia artificial y visualización. Para el desafío Earth System Trend Detective, buscamos transformar datos de ciencias de la Tierra de la NASA en una herramienta intuitiva para descubrir, analizar y explicar tendencias ambientales relevantes. Valoramos la rigurosidad científica, una ingeniería sólida, una experiencia de usuario clara y la resolución creativa de problemas.
summary:
Earth is changing, but detecting meaningful long-term trends across its complex systems remains a scientific challenge. Vast amounts of NASA Earth observation data are available, yet transforming them into accessible, interpretable, and reproducible evidence requires specialized tools.

TELLURIS, developed by Project Uriel, is a bilingual Earth-system investigation platform that transforms NASA data into interactive scientific explorations. It connects 18 NASA POWER environmental parameters, supports comparisons across locations and time, visualizes the planet using NASA imagery, and provides transparent statistical indicators, including trend estimates, uncertainty, and significance diagnostics.

The platform also integrates separate NASA natural-event and USGS earthquake catalogs to provide additional geographic context without implying unsupported causal relationships.

TELLURIS makes environmental evidence easier to explore, question, and communicate. Beyond climate research, its extensible architecture could support future investigations into vegetation, drought, environmental risks, and Earth-based research sites.

Our mission is simple: turn Earth observations into accessible scientific evidence, empowering more people to investigate our changing planet.
details:
TELLURIS — Investigate Earth. Question the Evidence.

1. The Problem

NASA provides decades of invaluable Earth-system observations and model-derived environmental data. However, interpreting long-term changes remains challenging. Scientific information is distributed across different services, geographic resolutions, measurement units, and temporal scales.

A visual trend does not automatically establish a statistically reliable change, and statistical significance does not establish causation.

We created TELLURIS to make this distinction more accessible.

2. Our Solution

TELLURIS is a bilingual, interactive Earth-system trend investigation platform developed by Project Uriel for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

It enables users to select environmental variables, investigate geographic locations, retrieve authentic NASA data, compare historical observations, and explore statistical evidence through an accessible scientific interface.

The implemented Explorer supports 18 NASA POWER environmental parameters and four investigation modes:

  • One parameter at one location.
  • One parameter compared across two locations.
  • Multiple parameters at one location.
  • Multiple parameters compared across two locations.

The platform includes a geographic 3D globe incorporating NASA GIBS imagery, interactive time-series charts, source-aware indicators, scientific explanations, and reproducible exports.

Additional interfaces provide separately identified NASA EONET natural-event reports and USGS earthquake catalog observations. These are used as geographic context, not as proof of relationships with climate trends.

3. Real NASA Data: Our Costa Rica Investigation

Our primary research case analyzes 41 complete calendar years of NASA POWER data, from 1985 through 2025, at two model-grid samples near Liberia and Limón, Costa Rica.

Using authentic NASA POWER meteorological records derived from MERRA-2, we investigated near-surface air temperature (T2M) and corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR).

The exploratory Theil–Sen temperature slope estimates are:

  • Liberia: −0.113 °C per decade.
  • Limón: +0.168 °C per decade.

These values are reproducible descriptive estimates, not definitive conclusions about regional climate change. Statistical interpretation remains conditional on temporal dependence, source-product consistency, and spatial representativeness.

Our analysis also revealed unusually large precipitation estimates requiring independent verification before physical interpretation.

A separate MODIS vegetation-data investigation identified an unsuitable coastal pixel near Limón through original land/water quality flags. Rather than hiding this negative result, we documented the issue and evaluated alternative research-site candidates.

These cases demonstrate a central TELLURIS principle: credible scientific investigation must recognize uncertainty and reject unreliable evidence.

4. Scientific Methodology

Our implementation combines:

  1. Original NASA data acquisition and source provenance.
  2. Parameter-specific units and temporal aggregation.
  3. Missing-data and completeness checks.
  4. Theil–Sen estimates of long-term change.
  5. Exploratory Mann–Kendall significance tests and confidence intervals.
  6. Serial-dependence and sensitivity diagnostics.
  7. Matched-calendar-year geographic comparisons.
  8. Reproducible JSON, CSV, and printable evidence reports.

Results are presented with documented methodological limitations. TELLURIS does not generate artificial scientific observations, infer causality from correlation, or treat historical trends as forecasts.

5. Technology and Engineering

The working prototype uses HTML5, CSS3, modular JavaScript, browser-based statistical calculations, Three.js for geographic visualization, and REST integrations with NASA POWER, NASA GIBS, NASA EONET, and the USGS earthquake service.

Python and SciPy support independent scientific reference calculations. Node.js tests and GitHub Actions provide automated quality assurance and reproducibility checks.

The platform is designed for lightweight static hosting, with Spanish and English interfaces and no mandatory user registration.

The EXP-013 source version passed 137 automated tests and local desktop/mobile Chromium acceptance checks. These engineering tests are separate from scientific validation and production-hosting verification.

6. Innovation and Creativity

TELLURIS combines several capabilities within one accessible research workflow:

  • Scientific evidence rather than visualization alone.
  • Geographic and multivariable comparison.
  • Explicit source provenance and methodological uncertainty.
  • An interactive Earth interface supported by authentic NASA imagery.
  • Deterministic explanations grounded in source-derived calculations.
  • A bilingual interface that makes environmental research more accessible.
  • Transparent separation of implemented capabilities and future research opportunities.

Our goal is not simply to display changing numbers, but to help users understand what the evidence supports, what remains uncertain, and which questions require further investigation.

7. Intended Impact and Future Applications

TELLURIS is designed for students, educators, citizen scientists, researchers, and communities seeking accessible Earth-system evidence.

Potential future applications include investigations into drought and water availability, vegetation and ecosystem change, environmental planning, disaster-related research context, and preliminary environmental characterization of terrestrial scientific or planetary-analog research sites.

Historical temperature, precipitation, and wind observations could also contribute contextual information to future aerospace research workflows, subject to dedicated scientific validation and mission-specific requirements.

TELLURIS is not an earthquake prediction system, an operational launch-weather tool, or a substitute for certified environmental assessments.

8. Responsible Development and Transparency

The project was developed during the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge with human-directed development and documented assistance from AI tools for research, coding, design, documentation, and audiovisual production.

All scientific observations are sourced from identifiable external datasets. Statistical calculations are deterministic and subject to reproducible checks. Generative AI is not connected to the current scientific interpretation engine.

Project decisions, experimental protocols, validation evidence, limitations, and external resource attributions are recorded in the project repository.

Conclusion

TELLURIS demonstrates how authentic NASA Earth data can become an accessible, transparent, and reproducible scientific investigation.

Because understanding our changing planet requires more than seeing a trend. It requires questioning the evidence.
